args.body:
PLAN DEVIATION REPORT
Bankruptcy Restructuring — Analyze Counterparty Markup of Plan of Reorganization
Matter File 4

Date: [Date of Report]
Prepared for: Client Deal Team
Re: Comparison of Creditors' Committee Redlined Plan Against Debtor's Original Plan of Reorganization

---

I. INTRODUCTION AND SCOPE

This deviation report compares the Creditors' Committee's redlined plan of reorganization (the "Committee Redline") against the debtor's original plan of reorganization (the "Original Plan"), as grounded in the operative deal materials, the attached valuation summary, the transmittal email, and the disclosure statement excerpts. The analysis identifies each material deviation introduced by the Committee Redline, assesses the deviation against the Original Plan and the applicable bankruptcy restructuring framework, and prioritizes the deviations consistent with the controlling deal team instruction.

The engagement instruction requires a plan-deviation-report.docx covering all deviations in the Committee Redline against the Original Plan, reconciled against the schedules, exhibits, valuation materials, and correspondence assembled in the matter file.

---

II. SOURCE DOCUMENTS REVIEWED

A. Original Plan and Base Materials (Matter Document ID 4): The debtor's original plan of reorganization, containing standard representations and warranties, covenants, conditions to confirmation, indemnification, and termination provisions.

B. Committee Redline — Counterparty Markup (Matter Document ID 30): The Creditors' Committee's revised plan of reorganization, accepting most firm-standard provisions but introducing targeted deviations in core economic and risk-allocation provisions.

C. Disclosure Statement Excerpts / Schedules and Exhibits (Matter Document ID 82): Disclosure schedules qualifying the base materials, including Schedule 3.7 (pending regulatory inquiries), Schedule 5.2 (retained liabilities), and Exhibit B (survival matrix).

D. Transmittal Email / Deal Correspondence (Matter Document ID 108): Partner email thread containing the controlling instruction on negotiation priorities: (i) the client will concede the basket conversion, and (ii) any survival-period reduction is treated as a walk-away issue.

E. Valuation Summary: Incorporated within the deal materials, providing the financial basis against which the Committee's economic modifications are assessed.

---

III. DEVIATION ANALYSIS

The Committee Redline introduces three material deviations from the Original Plan. Each is analyzed below in terms of (i) the nature of the change, (ii) its interaction with the disclosure statement schedules and exhibits, and (iii) its significance relative to the controlling client priorities.

---

A. Deviation No. 1 — Indemnification Cap Reduction and Basket Restructuring

1. Nature of the Deviation

   The Committee Redline silently reduces the aggregate indemnification cap from the level set forth in the Original Plan. Simultaneously, the Committee Redline converts the indemnification basket from a deductible structure (where the indemnitor bears the entire loss once the threshold is crossed) to a tipping basket structure (where only losses in excess of the basket threshold are recoverable).

2. Interaction with Schedules and Exhibits

   Schedule 5.2 of the disclosure statement lists retained liabilities that the Committee's indemnification restructuring would silently shift. By reducing the cap and converting the basket mechanism, the Committee Redline alters the risk allocation around those Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities. Any claim arising from a retained liability that previously fell within the scope of the deductible would now be borne by the debtor estate rather than the indemnifying party, while the reduced cap further narrows the aggregate exposure for the indemnifying party.

3. Assessment

   Per the controlling transmittal email instruction, the client will concede the basket conversion. The conversion from deductible to tipping basket is therefore a known and accepted concession.

   However, the reduction of the indemnification cap is a separate and distinct deviation. The controlling instruction does not authorize a cap reduction; authorized list reflects only the basket conversion. The cap reduction meaningfully narrows the indemnification protection available to the client for Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities and any other post-confirmation claims. This deviation must be flagged as material.

   The client should object to the cap reduction unless an acceptable compromise is reached. This deviation is counter to the client's interest because it reduces the maximum recoverable amount under the indemnification provisions without any corresponding concession identified in the transmittal email.

---

B. Deviation No. 2 — Material Adverse Effect (MAE) Carve-Outs for Regulatory Action

1. Nature of the Deviation

   The Committee Redline adds carve-outs to the definition of "Material Adverse Effect" for regulatory action "of exactly the kind at issue in this matter." This amendment narrows the scope of events that would constitute a Material Adverse Effect, thereby limiting the triggering conditions for protections tied to MAE.

2. Interaction with Schedules and Exhibits

   Schedule 3.7 of the disclosure statement discloses two pending regulatory inquiries. These inquiries intersect precisely with the carve-outs the Committee has added to the MAE definition. In other words, the Committee has drafted MAE carve-outs that would exclude — from the definition of MAE — regulatory consequences arising from the very inquiries already known and disclosed on Schedule 3.7.

   This is not a coincidence. The Committee Redline is calibrated to the known pending regulatory matters, such that adverse outcomes from those inquiries would be carved out of the MAE definition and would not constitute a Material Adverse Effect.

3. Assessment

   The MAE carve-out deviation is highly problematic. It would deprive the client of MAE protections precisely in the scenario where those protections are most needed: where pending regulatory inquiries result in material adverse regulatory outcomes. Schedule 3.7's disclosures highlight that the carve-outs are not abstract drafting points but rather directly targeted at the client's known regulatory exposure.

   The transmittal email does not authorize any concession on the MAE carve-outs. This deviation must be flagged as material and the client should reject the carve-outs in their current form. At a minimum, the carve-outs should be limited to exclude consequences arising from regulatory action not known or reasonably foreseeable at the time of the plan's confirmation.

---

C. Deviation No. 3 — Shortened Survival Period for Core Representations

1. Nature of the Deviation

   The Committee Redline introduces a new limitation period that shortens the survival of the core representation and warranty provisions. In contrast to the Original Plan's survival matrix, the Committee Redline reduces the applicable survival windows for the primary representations.

2. Interaction with Schedules and Exhibits

   Exhibit B to the disclosure statement sets forth the survival matrix. The Committee Redline's shortened limitation period directly contradicts the survival windows specified in Exhibit B. The schedules and exhibits state that "the scheduled exceptions control over general statements in the base bankruptcy restructuring materials." The survival matrix in Exhibit B therefore represents the operative survival terms, and the Committee Redline's new limitation period is inconsistent with that operative standard.

3. Assessment

   This is the most consequential deviation. Under the controlling transmittal email instruction, the client "treats any survival-period reduction as a walk-away issue." The survival period for core representations is a fundamental risk-allocation term, and shortening it materially undermines the client's ability to bring claims after confirmation.

   The shortened survival period contradicts Exhibit B's survival matrix, which the schedules state is controlling. Additionally, per the partner's directive in the transmittal email, any reduction in the survival period is a walk-away item — meaning the client is not prepared to entertain this deviation at all.

   The client should reject this deviation outright and require the Committee Redline to conform to the survival periods set forth in Exhibit B.

---

IV. PRIORITIZATION AND RECOMMENDATIONS

Consistent with the controlling transmittal email instruction and the disclosure statement schedules, the deviations are prioritized as follows:

| Priority | Deviation                        | Stance                        |
|----------|----------------------------------|-------------------------------|
| 1        | Survival period reduction        | WALK-AWAY — reject outright   |
| 2        | MAE carve-outs for regulatory    | REJECT — no concession        |
| 3        | Indemnification cap reduction    | REJECT — cap not addressed    |
| Conceeded| Basket conversion                | CONCEDE — accepted per email  |

A. Survival Period Reduction (Walk-Away):
   The client should treat the shortened survival period as a walk-away item per the controlling instruction. Counsel should require full restoration of the exhibit B survival matrix before proceeding further.

B. MAE Carve-Outs (Reject):
   The MAE carve-outs for regulatory action should be rejected. The carve-outs as drafted would exclude the Schedule 3.7 pending regulatory inquiries from MAE protection. Counsel should redraft any acceptable MAE carve-out to exclude only regulatory consequences not known or reasonably foreseeable at confirmation.

C. Indemnification Cap Reduction (Reject):
   The indemnification cap reduction should be rejected. The client conceded the basket conversion but does not concede any reduction in the overall indemnification cap. Counsel should require the cap to remain at the level set in the Original Plan.

D. Basket Conversion (Concede):
   The conversion from a deductible to a tipping basket is a conceded point per the controlling instruction and should not be re-litigated.

---

V. CONCLUSION

The Committee Redline introduces three material deviations from the Original Plan — a reduction of the indemnification cap, MAE carve-outs for regulatory action of the kind at issue, and a shortened survival period for core representations. Two of these deviations (the survival period reduction and the MAE carve-outs) intersect directly with disclosed schedules — Exhibit B (survival matrix) and Schedule 3.7 (pending regulatory inquiries) — that materially aggravate their impact on the client. The indemnification cap reduction operates in conjunction with Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities to shift risk away from the indemnifying parties.

Per the controlling transmittal instruction, the client will concede the basket conversion but must treat the survival-period reduction as a walk-away issue. Counsel should also reject the MAE carve-outs and the indemnification cap reduction as unauthorized deviations. The Committee Redline requires further negotiation on all three material deviations before the client can support confirmation of the plan.

---

Respectfully submitted,
Restructuring & Bankruptcy Practice Group
